title: Native pipes. Zero shell puzzles.
description: An input file becomes a line count through cat → tr → wc.
source:
# Purpose: Count lines after uppercasing a text file through native pipes.
# Input: input.txt in the calling directory. Output: native wc line count.
accept path as text with default "input.txt"
run "cat" with arguments [path]
pipe to "tr" with arguments ["[:lower:]", "[:upper:]"]
pipe to "wc" with arguments ["-l"]

title: Let grep be more than true or false.
description: Capture matching lines and the real native exit code, then save a report.
source:
# Search literal text in a file and save both native grep status and matching lines.
# 0 = matches, 1 = no matches, 2 = grep error. The report records all three.
accept path as text
accept pattern as text
accept report as text
run "grep" with arguments ["-n", "-F", "-e", pattern, "--", path] as matches and keep status as search_status
then "printf" with arguments ["grep exit: %s\n%s", search_status, matches]
then save to report

title: Keep the bytes moving.
description: A finite stream, native transformation and explicit record cutoff.
source:
# Finite native source, with output delivered one line at a time.
stream from printf with message "one\ntwo\nthree\nfour"
pipe to tr with from "[:lower:]" and to "[:upper:]"
take the first 3 lines
show each line

title: A whole CPU dashboard. One file.
description: ps supplies the numbers. The program defines layout, refresh, bars and table.
source:
# All application control flow is here. Rust supplies generic widgets and operations.
open a screen titled "Top 10 CPU processes"
divide the screen into two columns
place monitor on the left
place details on the right
give monitor 65 percent of the width
connect processes from monitor to processes in details

define a program named monitor
  offer processes as text

  show a heading named title with text "Top 10 by CPU usage"
  show a bar chart named usage
    label each bar from "label"
    size each bar from "cpu"
    label bar values with "%"
  show a badge named status with text "Waiting for a sample"
  show a button named refresh labelled "Refresh now"
  show a text panel named note with text "CPU values come from ps. Bars scale to the busiest process."

  whenever the program opens
    press refresh

  whenever key "Ctrl-R" is pressed
    press refresh

  whenever key "Ctrl-Q" is pressed
    close the screen

  every 2 seconds
    press refresh

  whenever refresh is pressed
    show "Sampling processes..." in status
    run ps with flags ["-A", "-o", "pid=", "-o", "pcpu=", "-o", "comm="]
    pipe to jq.ps with limit 10
    then show the result as bars in usage
    then send the result as processes
    then show "Live. Refreshes every 2 seconds." in status

  whenever a command fails
    show the error in status

define a program named details
  accept processes as text

  show a heading named title with text "Process details"
  show a table named records
    column "PID" from "pid"
    column "CPU %" from "cpu"
    column "Name" from "name"
  give records 14 rows
  show a text panel named note with text "PID identifies each process. CPU can exceed 100% for a process using several cores."

  whenever processes arrives
    show the result as rows in records

title: Stars, forks, and a little history.
description: gh supplies repository data; components communicate through explicit ports.
source:
# A single file: layout first, then each component's interface and behavior.
open a screen titled "GitHub star tracker"
divide the screen into two columns
place chooser on the left
place tracker on the right
give chooser 30 percent of the width
connect repository from chooser to repository in tracker

define a program named chooser
  offer repository as text

  show a heading named title with text "Repositories"
  show a text field named repo with value "morluto/rea"
  show a button named track labelled "Track repository"
  show a list named saved
    include "morluto/rea"
    include "cli/cli"
    include "ratatui/ratatui"

  whenever key "Ctrl-Q" is pressed
    close the screen

  whenever the program opens
    send the value of repo as repository

  whenever repo is submitted
    send the value of repo as repository

  whenever track is pressed
    send the value of repo as repository

  whenever an item is chosen in saved
    show that item in repo
    send that item as repository

define a program named tracker
  accept repository as text

  show a heading named title with text "Stars and forks"
  show a table named metrics
    column "Repository" from "nameWithOwner"
    column "Stars" from "stargazerCount"
    column "Forks" from "forkCount"
  show a line chart named history with key "nameWithOwner"
  label the horizontal axis of history "session seconds"
  label the vertical axis of history "stars"
  show a text panel named description
  show a badge named status with text "Waiting for a repository"
  show a button named refresh labelled "Refresh now"

  whenever repository arrives
    press refresh

  whenever key "Ctrl-R" is pressed
    press refresh

  every 60 seconds
    press refresh

  whenever refresh is pressed
    show "Refreshing..." in status
    run gh.repo with repository repository
    then show the result as rows in metrics
    then add field "stargazerCount" to history
    then show field "description" in description
    then show "Live data. Graph shows this session." in status

  whenever a command fails
    show the error in status

title: A tiny program with a pulse.
description: Stay alive and run a native command on a regular interval.

title: Structured without the subprocess shuffle.
description: Parse JSON and select typed fields inside the shared runtime.
source:
# Follow one JSON object per line; each object must have a text `name`.
accept path as text
listen to "tail" with arguments ["-n", "0", "-F", path]
whenever a line arrives as event
  then parse json as record
  take text at "/name" from record as name
  then "printf" with arguments ["%s\n", name]

title: English, meet Omarchy.
description: A positional summary becomes one literal argument to omarchy-shell.
source:
#!/usr/bin/env -S execute --
# Interface port of Omarchy v4.0.4; see README.md for compatibility limits.
accept arguments as list of text from arguments
accept summary as text from argument 1
run "omarchy-shell" with arguments ["-q", "notifications", "dismiss", summary]

title: The model decides a label. The program decides what happens.
description: A complete fixture-backed classification workflow with explicit confidence/evidence checks. Requires the repository fixtures and manifests.
source:
# Purpose: Build an evidence-linked incident timeline; prepare bounded evidence and save a review-only model-assisted report.
# Inputs: local source.json evidence, explicit model fixtures, and a private empty environment file.
# Outputs: out/incident-timeline.json; the workflow never changes the source evidence.
accept source_path as text with default "fixtures/001/source.json"
accept report_path as text with default "out/incident-timeline.json"
accept classify_fixture_path as text with default "fixtures/001/classify-evidence-ready.json"
accept draft_fixture_path as text with default "fixtures/001/draft.json"
accept generator_model as text with default "gpt-6-luna"
accept env_file as text with default ".env"
accept live as boolean with default false
# Refuse an output path that aliases an existing evidence or schema file.
run "test" with arguments ["!", source_path, "-ef", report_path]
run cat with path source_path
then jq with flags ["-c", "-S"] and filter "{incident,events:(.events|sort_by(.at))}" as evidence
if live is true
  then jev.classify with question "Do these time-ordered event records support drafting an incident timeline?" and labels ["evidence-ready", "insufficient-evidence"] and minimum 80 and env_file env_file as raw
otherwise
  then jev.classify with question "Do these time-ordered event records support drafting an incident timeline?" and labels ["evidence-ready", "insufficient-evidence"] and minimum 80 and fixture classify_fixture_path and env_file env_file as raw
then parse json as decision
take text at "/label" from decision as label
take boolean at "/accepted" from decision as accepted
take integer at "/confidence_percent" from decision as confidence
if accepted is true
  if label is "evidence-ready"
    run cat with path source_path
    then jq with flags ["-c", "-S"] and filter "{incident,events:(.events|sort_by(.at))}"
    if live is true
      then llm.ask with model generator_model and instruction "Draft a compact, timestamp-ordered incident timeline using only the supplied event records. Cite INC-104 and label causal links as unverified." and env_file env_file as draft_raw
    otherwise
      then llm.ask with model generator_model and instruction "Draft a compact, timestamp-ordered incident timeline using only the supplied event records. Cite INC-104 and label causal links as unverified." and fixture draft_fixture_path and env_file env_file as draft_raw
    then parse json as generated
    take text at "/text" from generated as draft
    run jq with flags ["-n", "-r", "-j", "--arg", "draft", draft, "--arg", "evidence", evidence] and filter "if ($draft | startswith(\"EVIDENCE:\")) and ([$evidence | scan(\"[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-[A-Z0-9-]+\") | . as $id | select($draft | contains($id))] | length > 0) then $draft else error(\"draft must start with EVIDENCE and cite an ID in bounded local evidence\") end" as validated_draft
    then "jq" with arguments ["-n", "-c", "-S", "--arg", "artifact", "incident_timeline", "--arg", "status", "draft-for-human-review", "--arg", "classification", label, "--argjson", "confidence", confidence, "--arg", "evidence", evidence, "--arg", "timeline_draft", validated_draft, "--arg", "action", "A human owner reviews this proposed analysis before acting.", "{artifact:$artifact,status:$status,confidence_percent:$confidence,evidence_excerpt:$evidence,timeline_draft:$timeline_draft,action:$action,classification:$classification}"]
    then save to report_path
  otherwise
    then "jq" with arguments ["-n", "-c", "-S", "--arg", "artifact", "incident_timeline", "--arg", "status", "needs-human-review", "--arg", "classification", label, "--argjson", "confidence", confidence, "--arg", "evidence", evidence, "--arg", "reason", "The accepted result did not match this workflow’s positive label, decision, or score level; generated analysis was withheld.", "--arg", "action", "An owner checks the original records and decides the next step.", "{artifact:$artifact,status:$status,confidence_percent:$confidence,evidence_excerpt:$evidence,timeline_draft:null,reason:$reason,action:$action,classification:$classification}"]
    then save to report_path
otherwise
  then "jq" with arguments ["-n", "-c", "-S", "--arg", "artifact", "incident_timeline", "--arg", "status", "needs-human-review", "--arg", "classification", label, "--argjson", "confidence", confidence, "--arg", "evidence", evidence, "--arg", "reason", "The model signal is below the configured 80 percent floor; no generated analysis was requested.", "--arg", "action", "An owner checks the original records and decides the next step.", "{artifact:$artifact,status:$status,confidence_percent:$confidence,evidence_excerpt:$evidence,timeline_draft:null,reason:$reason,action:$action,classification:$classification}"]
  then save to report_path
then cat with path report_path
